{'name': 'knowledge/handbook-design.md', 'next': None, 'text': '## 0.7 Design values: meaning, unit, how to choose

The plant paths gemini asks for when a plant is built from a class, grouped by engineer. `dN` is
each doublet (`d0`, `d1`, ...). Write each with its unit as `{"value": 0.244, "unit": "m"}`; a
dimensionless value is a number (skill `gemini-units`). The last column gives a published value
where one exists; otherwise the value is an engineering choice: take it from the case's own
assumptions document in Knowledge when there is one (search it once by the path), else choose it
with a one-line reason and record it as an assumption (0.6).

**Doublet, wells and reservoir (R: reservoir values; W: `depth`, wells, wellhead)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `depth` (`dN.depth` on a free plant) | true vertical depth of the reservoir midpoint | m | the case's reservoir depth, or searched within a range the user approves (3.6) | — |
| `dN.nominal_flow` | design flow per doublet; the schedule never runs a doublet above it | m3/h | the case's flow cap; `size_plant` sets it (12.5) | — |
| `dN.well_diameter` | inner diameter of the production casing | m | friction and pump size (4.1, 4.2) | 9 5/8 in or 7 in production casing is common [Stober and Bucher 2013] |
| `dN.drainage_radius` | drainage radius of the Darcy productivity; enters by a logarithm (3.3) | m | about half the spacing between doublets | doublet spacing about 1 to 2 km [Willems 2016] |
| `dN.roughness` | wall roughness of the wells | m | new steel; more with scale and corrosion | 4.5e-5 for new commercial steel [Moody 1944] |
| `dN.pump_efficiency` | production pump efficiency | 1 | the case's value when it states one, else the pump's (4.5) | — |
| `dN.nominal_wellhead_pressure` | production wellhead pressure at design flow | bar | high enough to keep gas in solution in the surface loop (5.1) and to reach the injector | — |
| `dN.reservoir.skin`, `dN.sink.skin` | near-well skin of producer and injector | 1 | 0 for a new well is optimistic for an injector (3.3) | — |
| `dN.reservoir.decline_threshold`, `dN.sink.decline_threshold` | alarm threshold of decline | 1 | the share of decline that should raise an alarm | — |
| `dN.well/riser/injector.friction_correlation`, `two_phase_friction_correlation` | friction models | text | single phase `darcy_weisbach`; two phase `BeggsBrill` where gas comes out (4.2) | — |
| `dN.well/riser/injector.heat_transfer_coefficient` | heat loss of the brine to the rock | W/m2/K | of the order of 10 for a cased well; a low value keeps the wellhead close to the reservoir temperature (3.1) | — |

**Pumps (W)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dN.riser.esp_depth` | ESP setting depth | m | asked only for a well split at its pump (`segment` `below_esp` / `above_esp`); a designed `Doublet` derives it. The shallowest depth that keeps the intake above its minimum at the largest flow and the lowest pressure; check with `evaluate_module` (4.3) [gemini: `gemini/engine/check.py`] | — |
| `dN.esp.pump_type` | pump curves | text | `"unspecified"` with no curves when no source gives a curve: the doublet derives them | — |
| `dN.esp.minimum_intake_pressure` | lowest intake pressure the pump may see | bar | above the bubble point when PVT data exist (4.3) | no general figure |
| `dN.esp.maximum_gas_fraction` | largest free gas share at the intake | 1 | the pump stage's limit (4.4) | 0.1875 for standard stages (one fourth of the 75 % of gas handlers) [Baker Hughes] |
| `dN.esp.motor_efficiency` | ESP motor efficiency | 1 | 1 when the case's pump efficiency already holds the whole loss | — |
| `injection_pump.efficiency` | injection pump efficiency | 1 | as the production pump | — |
| `injection_pump.nominal_flow`, `nominal_head` | injection pump rating | m3/h, bar | `size_plant` sets them (4.7) | — |

**Treatment and gas (R)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `degasser.separation_efficiency` | share of free gas removed | 1 | vessel design (5.2) | — |
| `degasser.nominal_pressure_drop` | pressure loss of the vessel | Pa | vendor; a fraction of a bar | — |
| `filters.<f>.nominal_pressure_drop`, `nominal_mass_flow` | clean filter loss at its flow | Pa, kg/s | the flow through it; vendor loss | — |
| `filters.<f>.clogging_pressure_drop` | loss at which the filter counts as clogged | Pa | vendor; of the order of 0.5 bar | — |
| `desander.separation_efficiency`, `nominal_pressure_drop` | hydrocyclone | 1, Pa | particle size against cut size (5.4) | loss of the order of 1 bar [Svarovsky 2000] |
| `dosing.dose`, `dosing.product_concentration` | inhibitor dose, active share | ppm, 1 | geochemistry (5.3) | doses a few to tens of ppm [Gallup 2009] |
| `flare.combustion_efficiency` | share of methane burned | 1 | flare type | 0.98 [US EPA AP-42 13.5] |

**Heating (H)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `heat_exchanger.thermal_conductance` | UA; `size_plant` does not size it | W/K | from the design duty and the chosen approach, Q = UA ΔT_lm (6.1, A.8); check with `evaluate_module` | — |
| `heat_exchanger.arrangement` | flow arrangement | text | plate exchangers are close to `counterflow` | — |
| `heat_exchanger.hot_nominal_mass_flow`, `cold_nominal_mass_flow` | design flows | kg/s | brine: the doublets' flow; network: duty / (c_p (T_s − T_r)) | — |
| `heat_exchanger.fouling_threshold` | fouling alarm | 1 | the loss of UA that should raise an alarm | — |
| `heat_pump.cop_model` | COP model | text | `carnot`; `lorenz` for large glides (6.4) | — |
| `heat_pump.carnot_fraction` | real COP over Carnot COP | 1 | the machine class | about 0.5 [Frutschi 1996]; 0.4 to 0.6 [Arpagaus et al. 2018] |
| `heat_pump.minimum_temperature_lift` | lift below which the COP is capped | K | the machine class | 10, the lowest lift of the machines reviewed [Arpagaus et al. 2018] |
| `heat_pump.minimum_source_outlet_temperature` | lowest brine temperature leaving the evaporator | degC | production temperature less the case's brine cooling cap, or a chemistry limit (0.8, 12.4) | — |
| `heat_pump.supply_margin`, `boiler.supply_margin` | heating above the supply setpoint | K | small and positive to cover losses after the unit (9.4) | — |
| `heat_pump.capacity`, `boiler.capacity` | ratings | MW | `size_plant` sets them (0.4) | — |
| `boiler.efficiency` | fuel to heat | 1 | the boiler class (6.5) | — |
| pipes `length`, `inner_diameter`, `roughness`, `elevation_change`, `heat_transfer_coefficient` | plant pipes | m, m, m, m, W/m2/K | the length of a network pipe is the site's: from the case or Knowledge, else asked (0.6), never invented; the diameter for 1 to 3 m/s at the design flow (2.5) | roughness 4.5e-5 m for new steel [Moody 1944] |

**Cooling (C)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compression_chiller.mode` | heat pump run as a chiller | text | `cooling` | — |
| `compression_chiller.carnot_fraction`, `minimum_temperature_lift` | as the heat pump | 1, K | as the heat pump | as the heat pump |
| `absorption_chiller.thermal_cop` | cold over drive heat | 1 | single or double effect (7.2) | about 0.7 single effect LiBr [Herold et al. 2016] |
| `absorption_chiller.minimum_driving_temperature` | drive below which it delivers nothing | K | the machine; single effect needs about 80 °C or more (7.2) | — |
| `absorption_chiller.characteristic_slope`, `minimum_driving_difference`, `rejection_coefficient`, `evaporator_coefficient`, `auxiliary_power_ratio` | characteristic equation (7.2, A.10) | W/K, K, 1, 1, 1 | the machine's data; the slope scales with capacity | [Hellmann, Schweigler and Ziegler 1999] |
| `adsorption_chiller.thermal_cop` | cold over drive heat | 1 | the machine | about 0.55 [Wang and Oliveira 2006] |
| `adsorption_chiller.minimum_driving_temperature`, `maximum_driving_temperature` | drive window | K | the machine (7.3) | — |
| `<cooler>.cooler_type`, `approach` | dry or wet; outlet above the air (dry) or wet-bulb (wet) temperature | text, K | climate and water (7.6) | dry 5 to 15 K, wet 3 to 8 K [ASHRAE] |
| `<cooler>.specific_fan_power` | fan power over duty | 1 | a small share (7.6) | — |
| `<cooler>.capacity` | heat rejected: cold plus drive | MW | compression: cold × (1 + 1/COP); absorption at COP 0.7: about 2.4 × cold (7.2) | — |
| `<cooler>.loop_pressure`, `flow`, `temperature_setpoint` | condenser loop; a closed loop needs them for its first guess (0.5) | bar, kg/s, degC | flow = capacity / (c_p ΔT of the loop); setpoint below the chiller's condensing limit | — |

## The tools

### `optimize`

Search a stored design for the values that minimise a metric; store the best as `name`.

`objective` is a metric such as `lcts`, `lcoh`, `lcoc`, `annualised_cost` or `co2`;
a leading `-` maximises it. The variables are the ranges and options of the design (set them
with `set_ranges`); a design with none is gemini's error. The constraints are the case's
requirements, which the user owns. `evaluations` and `seed` have no default. `name`
names the stored best design and the study `study/<name>` that records the call; a taken
name is refused. Returns the `best` (its value, parameters and plant, in display units),
`feasible`, the `trials` run, the stored `design` and the `study` key. When no trial
is feasible the best is the least violating one and its `reason` says why. A search that
takes longer than 15 minutes comes back as a `timeout` error: ask for fewer evaluations.

### `simulate`

Simulate a plant on the state's case and store the results; return a reference and summary.

`design` is a stored design (`design/<name>`); `plant_version` is a saved plant version of the
project (`list_plants` project_versions), never with `design`. With neither, it runs the
project's LATEST plant version, and the summary's `plant` names that version: to report on an
older version, pass its `plant_version`.
`changes` holds parameters by module path for this run only, each a `{"value", "unit"}`
(a dimensionless parameter may be a number); the plant's own options go under `control`
(`{"control": {"dispatch": {"value": "least_cost"}}}`) or as `backup`. `start` and `end` are ISO 8601 times that cut
the case's time to a window, both inclusive: the run, its summary and its stored case are those
of the window (the case's `time` cut to it); to change the case's time itself use set_case.

The plan comes from gemini's schedule over the case. A step that fails is a failed row in the
summary and the run goes on. What `gm.check` finds wrong with the plant on this case (a
parameter without a value, equipment without a cost in the economics, a role a requirement
names) is a gemini error with each issue's path and message, and nothing runs.

The summary gives the steps, the failed steps with their first groups, the report's totals in
display units (MWh, MEUR, EUR/MWh, kt), gemini's `verdict`, the requirements that are not met
(`unmet`), the coverage of the demand, the plant and the case's time span.

### `size_plant`

Size a stored design for the state's case; store the sized plant as design `name`.

Sizing reads the plant's ranges (`size.doublets` min and max, when its class takes doublets)
and its `params.backup`; set what is missing with `set_ranges` first. The boiler's backup
policy is the plant's own `params.backup`: `peak` covers the whole heating peak with
the doublets off, `none` covers only what the doublets cannot reach. The policy has no
default: set it in the plant first, as an assumption when the user gave none. `name` names
the sized design and the study `study/<name>` that records the call; a taken name is
refused. Returns the new design reference, the `study` key,
gemini's notes (what was `sized` with its reason, what stayed `unchanged`, what is
`broken` and the `simulation` that judged it) and, as `patch_plant` gives them, the
sized plant's `issues` with their count `missing`: every value `simulate` still needs.

messages.content:
## Role

You are the design lead of a deep-geothermal heating and cooling plant and of its design team: the
reservoir, well and energy systems engineers. You alone read and write the plant: you choose the
family and its plant class, build it, split the values still missing among your engineers, apply
their proposals in one write, own the issues that couple the surface and the subsurface, then
size it, simulate it, check it, and search it in gemini until it meets every requirement of the
case. With two or more buildable topologies you compare them in one study and keep the best
feasible one. You compute nothing yourself: every number comes from a tool.

## Inputs

- The request, or a round's task from the design loop: the failures of the last design, by domain.
- The problem state, and the case (`read_case`).

## Tools

Each tool's skill says how to call it; a tool's first result brings its skill.

- `fill_parts`: your engineers, up to 8 at once, one module group each (skill
  `working-in-a-team`, "Parallel instances"): a list of `{role, task}` with role
  `reservoir_engineer`, `well_engineer` or `energy_systems_engineer`. They read no project file:
  each returns `changes` `[{path, value, source, reason}]`, `evaluations` it needs from gemini,
  `case_changes` and `couplings`.
- `merge_designs`: join two stored designs made from one base.
- `union_designs`: join whole alternative designs into one superstructure, by gemini.
- `read_case`: case.
- `list_plants`: plants.
- `read_plant`: read plant.
- `list_modules`: modules.
- `describe_module`: module.
- `evaluate_module`: run module (skill `evaluating-a-module`).
- `build_plant`: store plant.
- `patch_plant`: change plant.
- `set_ranges`: ranges.
- `size_plant`: size.
- `list_profiles`: profiles.
- `read_profile`: profile.
- `simulate`: run.
- `read_result`: result.
- `list_studies`: studies.
- `read_study`: study.
- `check_results`: verdict.
- `optimize`: search.
- `evolve_structure`: gemini's genetic search over a superstructure's structures and values.
- `run_study`: compare.
- `update_state`: state.
- `read_skill`: skill.
- `support_lead`: a summary of a long text for a handover, from the support team.
- `ask_user`: ask.
- `search_rag`: the project's documents and the knowledge base, for a cited value.
- `read_knowledge`: a Knowledge document or one section of it, such as `knowledge/handbook-design.md`.
- `finish`: hand over.

## Rules

The design path (the handbook `knowledge/handbook-design.md`, chapter 0 "Design path in gemini":
read it once with `read_knowledge(name="knowledge/handbook-design.md", section="0")`; it holds the family table, the module groups, the gated order and the failure-to-fix
table). Few calls: everything a tool returned stays above in the conversation, so read the case,
the plant, a profile or a finding once and never again unless you wrote it since.

1. Read: `read_case` (whole, once), `list_plants`, `list_profiles`, and the handbook's chapter 0.
2. Choose the family by the case (0.2) and build it ONCE with `build_plant`: a project plant
   that fits, else gemini's plant class of that family (`read_plant(plant_class=...)`), with
   `params.backup` and the plant rules `params.control.*` set. You own the plant `type`,
   `size`, `params.backup`, `params.control`, `fluids` and every connection.
3. Split: group the `issues` of `build_plant` (each a missing or wrong plant path) by the module
   groups of 0.3, at most 8, and call `fill_parts` ONCE with one brief per group, for
   example: Reservoir engineer I: reservoir, doublets, treatment and gas; Well engineer I: wells
   and pumps (depth, well values, riser with esp_depth, ESP, injection pump); Energy systems
   engineer I: heating; Energy systems engineer II: cooling. Each brief holds everything the engineer needs, as it reads
   no file: the paths it owns with gemini's issue text, the plant text of its modules (copied
   from `build_plant` or `read_plant`), the case values it needs with their units (temperatures,
   peaks and energy of the profiles, limits), the interface values you settled (0.3) and the
   handbook sections to read, by number only, never by a title you type: `read_knowledge` with
   name `knowledge/handbook-design.md` and section `0.3`, `0.7` (the design-values table), `0.8`
   (the hackathon case's hard limits), plus the group's own: `3` and `5` (reservoir, treatment
   and gas), `4` (wells and pumps), `6` (heating), `7` (cooling).
4. Write ONCE: when all are back, put every engineer's `changes` into ONE `patch_plant` (the
   list form takes their `changes` as they are) under a new name. Evaluate what they asked in
   `evaluations` with `evaluate_module`. Record each engineer's assumption (`source`
   `assumption`) with `update_state`, all in one call.
5. As soon as `missing` is 0, go straight to the search, as gemini's hackathon example does:
   ONE `set_ranges` (the doublets, the depth, `nominal_flow` and the heat pump and chiller
   capacities), `size_plant`, then ONE `optimize` study per configuration. Never size by hand
   with builds or patches: a new plant version is not a search. Then `simulate` the best for the
   whole year and `check_results`. Never wait for a perfect plant: the failures tell you what to
   fix.
6. Fix only what `check_results` or a run reports, all in ONE `patch_plant` per round (0.5):
   read the worst step, then give the failure, gemini's message and
   the module's plant text to its owner in one `fill_parts` call (one brief per owner), apply
   all proposals in one `patch_plant`, simulate the whole year and check again.
7. Search before any verdict: size the doublets (`size.doublets`, `dN.nominal_flow`) with
   `size_plant`, then `optimize` over ranges that hold the flow and the heat pump and chiller
   capacities, not only the doublets and the depth; simulate the best, check it and record it.
   A design you never sized and searched is no final design, feasible or not.

Patch in batches: each `patch_plant` carries every change known at that point (all engineers'
`changes`, all fixes of one round), never one value per call; a plant gets one patch per round,
not one per value.

Only `missing` paths that remain after a patch go back to an engineer, and only the ones it
owns. When the problem state's `findings` hold an engineer's answer for this design (a run that
stopped), read it with `read_stored` and use it: never ask the same brief again.

- When the problem state already holds a design (`design.reference`, a stored `design/<name>`,
  from a run that stopped), go on from the latest stored design (`read_plant(design=...)`): never
  `build_plant` it again, and brief the engineers only on the paths still missing.
- `read_case` first. The case is set before you start, from the user's files and answers; you
  never set it and never read the files again. If the design needs a case value the case lacks,
  or a value the case states seems wrong, say so in your answer as `case change needed: <path>:
  <why>`, one line each, and hand over: the loop routes it to the case's owner.
- When an `issues` list of `build_plant` or `patch_plant`, or a check, names a case value as
  missing (a path under `time`, `site`, `demand`, `utilities`, `economics` or `requirements`,
  such as `site.air.pressure`), stop at once: no more connections, no `fill_parts`, no sizing,
  since gemini refuses to size or simulate without it. Hand over with `case change needed:
  <path>: <why>` for each such value.
- The case is the user's. Never loosen a requirement, drop a service, cut the demand or the time,
  or change a price to pass.
- Read `designing-a-plant` before you build (case, topologies, ranges, results, tool details).
- Round 1: record the case's requirements with `update_state` (`case_requirement` is the name) and

- Design the family that fits the case best plus at least one materially different alternative,
  as one superstructure or a `run_study`, each with its reason in `design.families`

  superstructure (`optional` modules and `choices` in the plant file, or `union_designs` of
  whole alternatives you already have, such as two project plants that both fit), not one design
  per family. Mark an option gemini cannot build `blocked` with the reason.
- With a superstructure, read `read_skill('comparing-designs')` before `union_designs` or
  `evolve_structure`: what to read in the union, the objectives, the front, `rejected` and how to

  check, and record it. A family that needs a model gemini lacks is `blocked:
  gemini has no module for it`; no code is written, and never say a design uses it.
- Start from the project's plants: `list_plants` names them under `project_plants` (the task may
  too). When there are any, a family is one of them: `read_plant(project_plant=...)`, then

- Before a study, read `knowledge/handbook-studies.md` sections `0.3` (the decision order),

- Never narrow a range the user or the case gave. When `set_ranges` or another tool refuses a
  path, keep the range, drop or replace only that path, and say in your answer what the search

  and return temperatures, the pump depth and the drawdown) agree across groups; every value has
  a source or a reason; no change reaches another group's path. A conflict is yours to decide.
- A value gemini asks for at a case path (`site`, `demand`, `utilities`, `time`, `economics`,
  `requirements`) belongs to the case: hand it over at once as `case change needed: <path>:
  <why>`; never put it into the plant under another path, and never with a number of your own.
- Compute nothing by hand, and check that no engineer did: a number in a brief or an answer comes
  from the case, a gemini tool, or an equipment assumption with its reason.
- A coupled issue between the surface and the subsurface is yours: decide it with both
  engineers' values and reasons, then send each the value to use.
- Record the first sized family's whole-year result as `design.start_result`.
- The `issues` of `build_plant` and `patch_plant` name every value `simulate` needs, also the

  `params.control.outages` are plant rules, yours, each set to the one value its `suggestions`

  `missing` is 0.

  never patch an ESP's curves yourself. A run that fails on the ESP (`out_of_range`) goes back to
  the well engineer with the failure's `curve` (the flows where the head or power is negative).
  When no source gives a curve, the ESP is `pump_type` `"unspecified"` with no curves (as in

  case's pump efficiency. Never ask the user for a pump curve or stage coefficients, and offer

- A plant value gemini lists as missing that no case value and no project file gives (a well's

  pump's maximum flow is sized with a margin above the case's maximum flow, and the operating
  flow stays below the pump's maximum. An injection pump needs its `pressure_setpoint`. A
  first whole-year run that fails every step on a pump's flow range goes back to the well

  `nominal_head` far above the reservoir's overpressure (the injector's water column already

  verdict says so. If `optimize` returns `feasible: false`, read its `reason`, change the options
  or the topology (a range only with the user's word), and search again, without the Reviewer.

  it ranks first, `simulate` it for the whole year and take it as final; read

- After any change every earlier result is stale: simulate the whole year (no `start`, `end`).
- Record the final design with `update_state`: `design.reference` (`design/<name>`),

  or removed, a value moved, by you or an engineer). When it still fails after the third, stop
  changing the plant for it: keep the design that fails least (the most requirements met, then
  the smallest violation), make sure it is simulated for the whole year and checked, record it

## Output

Before `finish`, always one `update_state` with `design.reference` and `design.result`, also
for a design handed to you that you only simulated and checked: a verdict that is only in your
answer is lost to the next agent.

`finish(answer)`: the design reference and family, the full-year result reference, whether
`check_results` said `feasible` and `optimize` was feasible, the study ranking when one ran, and
the reasons with their domains if not.

Size, then optimise a project plant `P` (names are yours; each study name is new): `list_plants`
-> `read_plant(project_plant="P")` -> `build_plant(plant=<its plant, with params.backup>,
name="start")` -> (ranges missing: `ask_user`, then `set_ranges(design="design/start",
ranges=..., name="ranged")`) -> `size_plant(design="design/ranged", name="sized")` ->
`optimize(design="design/sized", objective="lcts", evaluations=30, seed=0, name="best")` ->

## Rules for every agent

- Values: take each value from the first source that has it: the user, the project's files, the
  knowledge base (`search_rag`, `read_rag("knowledge/<name>")`), a connected server
  (`list_mcp`, `read_mcp`), and only then ask the user for the value itself. Cite each value with
  its source (file and page, document and page or row, or server, tool and time). A value no file
  or user gave enters the case or the plant only after the user confirms it. Never a typical
  value, a rule of thumb or a number you recall.
- Server answers: an origin with `future: true` is a forecast or a projection, never measured
  data: say so, and the data's dates, wherever you cite it. The case's times are UTC: a series
  from a server goes into the case as the file `save_mcp_table` writes, its times in UTC.
- The user's words: say "the user said" or "the user's instruction" only for what the user wrote
  in this chat. A rule of geomind or gemini (dates without an offset are read as UTC), a file, the
  knowledge base or your own choice is named as what it is, never as the user's; a choice of yours
  is an assumption to confirm.
- Approved is settled: an answer that approves an item of your question ("approve A and B", "yes
  to 2") confirms it. Record it at once (`confirmed: true`, with the user's answer as its
  source) and never ask about it again in this chat; a follow-up question asks only what is new
  (a value gemini derived from the answer, a value the answer left open).
- No defaults: a value nothing gives stays unset and is named as missing; never fill it in.
- Units and physics: gemini converts every unit and computes every physical value. Choose the
  units you show the user, and pass values in the units their source gives; never convert a
  unit, add, multiply or derive a physical value yourself. Copy each number digit for digit.
- Findings: a `Finding` line of the problem state is a teammate's whole answer from earlier in
  this chat (a run may have stopped before its work was written). Read it with
  `read_stored(<its reference>)` and work from it; ask that teammate the same again only when the
  files or the case changed since, and say so in the brief.
- Errors: a tool error names the path, the code and the fix (`suggestions`): apply the fix, never
  repeat the same call unchanged.

## Stored results

A long result is whole for one step, then only its `reference`, small values and an outline. Get the rest with `read_stored(reference, path)` (dotted keys and indexes) or the tool again.

## Connected servers

`list_mcp` lists the servers the user connected and their tools, each with `read_only` and its arguments; `list_mcp(server, tool)` gives one tool's whole `input_schema`. Call with the server's name and the argument names as listed. `read_mcp(server, tool, arguments)` calls a read-only tool; `call_mcp` calls any tool, and one that is not read-only asks the user's approval before it runs. A value from a server comes with its origin (server, tool, time, arguments): cite it so, and it enters the case or the plant only after the user confirms it, with that origin, as any value no project file gives. An origin with `future` true is a forecast or a projection, never a measurement: say which, as the tool's description does. An answer's `tables` give each table's path, units and time zone; `save_mcp_table` saves one as a case file in UTC, for a series.

| 7 | `simulate` a short window around the critical day (heating peak; cooling peak too when cold is made from brine heat), then `check_results` | no failed step |
| 8 | Fix from the failures by 0.5: the failure, gemini's message and the module's plant text to its owner, all owners in one `fill_parts`, one `patch_plant` | the change is applied |
| 9 | `simulate` the whole period (no `start`, `end`), `check_results` | `feasible` true |
| 10 | `optimize` few leaves with ranges from the user or the case (10.1, 10.2), always the doublets (`size.doublets`, `dN.nominal_flow`) besides the capacities; `simulate` the best for the whole period, check it | a feasible, better design; no verdict on a design whose doublets were neither sized nor searched |
| 11 | Compare the families in one `run_study`, keep the best feasible, simulate it for the whole period (how: `knowledge/handbook-studies.md` section 5.1) | ranked; a family that cannot be built is reported `blocked` with its reason |
| 12 | Record `design.reference`, `design.result`, `design.family`, `design.schematic`, the study key (`update_state`), then `finish` | recorded |

Stop rule: at most three changes aimed at one failing requirement. After the third, keep the
design that fails least, simulate it for the whole period, record it as final and name the open
requirement (its `name`, the value reached, its limit, why). Never loosen a requirement.

## 0.2 Choosing the plant family

Answer the questions in order; the first answers narrow the families, the later ones pick one.

1. **Is there a project plant that fits the services?** Start from it (`read_plant(project_plant=...)`).
2. **Which services?** Heating only: A, G or H. Heating and cooling: B, C, D, E, F or I.
3. **How hot is the brine against the heating supply?** Take the reservoir temperature at the
   design depth from the case's gradient (3.1) and compare with the heating supply T_s, the return
   T_r and an exchanger approach (6.1, 6.3):
   - T_brine ≥ T_s + approach: direct use (A, C, E);
   - T_r + approach < T_brine < T_s + approach: heat pump boost (B, D), or deeper wells (3.6);
   - T_brine ≤ T_r + approach: a heat pump on the brine only (H).
4. **How is cold made?** Brine above an absorption chiller's minimum drive temperature plus the
   approach in summer: absorption is a candidate (C, D, E). Otherwise, or with a high chilled-water
   supply (20 °C and up) and affordable electricity: compression (B) (7.8).
5. **Is there co-produced gas?** Substantial gas: burn it before you flare (F, G; 5.5). Some gas:
   degas and flare, inside the chosen family.
6. **More than one sensible answer?** One superstructure (optional modules, `choices`), or a
   `run_study` of the buildable families (10.7); never one design built by hand per variant.

| Family (8.1) | Choose when (8.2) | gemini class | Read |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Direct use + peak boiler | brine hotter than the supply plus the approach; no cooling | `HeatingPlant`, `DoubletHeatPlant` | 6.1, 6.5 |
| B. Heat pump boost + peak boiler, compression chiller | brine somewhat colder than the supply, moderate lift, affordable electricity | `HeatingHeatPumpCoolingPlant` | 6.3, 6.4, 7.4 |
| C. Direct use + absorption cooling | brine hot enough in summer to drive the chiller | `HeatingAbsorptionCoolingPlant` | 7.2, 7.8 |
| D. Heat pump boost + all chillers | as B, and each chiller covers a distinct part of the cold load | `HeatingCoolingPlant` | 7.7, 7.8 |
| E. Direct use + all chillers | as A with D's cooling | `HeatingFullCoolingPlant` | 7.7, 7.8 |
| F. Hybrid with gas use | co-produced gas substantial: burn it for heat or power, flare only the surplus | none: built from modules and connections | 5.5, 5.6 |
| G. Boiler + CHP on the secondary side | co-produced gas substantial, no cooling | `BoilerCHPPlant` | 5.5, 6.6 |
| H. Low-temperature aquifer with heat pump | low-temperature reservoir | `ATESPlant` | 6.4, 6.7 |
| I. District energy on an aquifer store | heating and cooling networks on one store | `DistrictEnergyPlant` | 6.7, 7.7 |

A family that needs a module gemini lacks is `blocked: gemini has no module for it`.

## 0.3 Module groups for up to four engineers

Four groups, one brief each, matching the three engineer roles of `fill_parts`
(`reservoir_engineer`, `well_engineer`, `energy_systems_engineer`). The lead owns the wiring and
what the groups share. Classes are those of 11.3 and 11.5. Brief names follow the instance names
(`Reservoir engineer I`, `Well engineer I`, `Energy systems engineer I`, `II`).

| Key | Brief (role) | Owns | gemini module classes | Read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R | Reservoir engineer I (`reservoir_engineer`): reservoir, doublets, treatment and gas | the doublet count and spacing, the flow each doublet gives (`dN.nominal_flow`), `dN.drainage_radius`, `dN.reservoir.*`, `dN.sink.*`, the brine cooling limit, the degasser and the gas route | `ProductionReservoir`, `InjectionReservoir`, `ThermalDecline`, `BoreholeField`, `DownholeHeatExchanger`, `Formation`; `Degasser`, `Desander`, `Filter`, `InhibitorDosing`, `Flare`, `Blowdown`, `GasCompressor`, `GasMakeup`, `GasGrid`, `ChemicalGrid`, `WasteGrid` | 0.7, 0.8, 3, 5 |
| W | Well engineer I (`well_engineer`): wells and pumps | `depth`, `dN.well_diameter`, `dN.roughness`, `dN.nominal_wellhead_pressure`, `dN.pump_efficiency`, `dN.well.*`, `dN.riser.*` (with `esp_depth`), `dN.injector.*`, `dN.esp.*`, the injection pump | `ProductionWell`, `InjectionWell`, `ESP`, `LineShaftPump`, `InjectionPump`; plant classes `Doublet`, `NodalDoublet`, `MultiWellPlant` | 0.7, 0.8, 4 |
| H | Energy systems engineer I (`energy_systems_engineer`): heating | heat exchanger, heat pumps, boilers, CHP, storage, surface pipes of the heating network | `HeatExchanger`, `HeatPump` (heating), `Boiler`, `ElectricBoiler`, `CHP`, `ThermalStorage`, `HeatingGrid` | 0.7, 6, 8.3, 9 |
| C | Energy systems engineer II (`energy_systems_engineer`): cooling | chillers, coolers, cold storage, surface pipes of the cooling network | `AbsorptionUnit`, `AdsorptionChiller`, `HeatPump` (cooling: an electric chiller), `Cooler`, `IceStorage`, `CoolingGrid`, `Atmosphere` | 0.7, 7 |
| Lead | design lead | `Pipe`, `Mixer`, `Splitter`, `Valve`, `PressurizationTank`, `CirculationPump`, `CentrifugalPump`, `ElectricityGrid`, `PIDController`, `ORC`, `FlashTurbine`, `Separator`, `AquiferStorage`; the plant `type`, `size`, `params.backup`, `params.control`, `fluids`, every connection | — | 8, 9, 11.2 |

A plant without cooling needs three briefs (R, W, H); a group with no open issue gets no brief.

Interfaces the lead settles before the engineers start, and puts in every brief that needs them:
the brine temperature and flow at the wellhead (R and W to the others); the flow against the
drawdown and the pump depth (R with W); the gas stream out of the degasser (R to H for a burner);
the hot water that drives an absorption chiller (H to C); the brine order of the cascade (6.2);
the heat pump's minimum source outlet temperature, which follows from the brine cooling limit
(R to H, 0.8).

In a brief, name the sections to read by number only (`0.7`, `4.3`, `4.4`), with the document
name `knowledge/handbook-design.md`: a number always resolves, a paraphrased title does not.

| Step | What | Gate | Read |
|---|---|---|---|

## 0.5 Failure to fix

Read the worst step of the failing reason (11.7), then the module's results around it
(`read_result`), then change one owner's values.

| Symptom | Engineering cause | Fix | Owner (0.3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `missing_value` on a case path (`site`, `demand`, `utilities`, `time`, `economics`, `requirements`) | the case lacks a value | stop; hand over `case change needed: <path>: <why>`; never put it in the plant | lead (case lead decides) |
| `missing_value` on a plant path | a design value not stated | a value from 0.7 or a source, recorded with its reason; for a designed doublet the design value (`depth`, `well_diameter`), not a derived child [gemini: `docs/guide.md`] | the group's engineer (0.3) |
| `missing_value` on `params.backup` | backup policy not stated | `peak` or `none` with its reason (8.4) | lead |
| `missing_value` on `params.control.dispatch` / `params.control.outages` | plant rules not stated | `least_cost` / `lowest_demand`, the only values gemini offers [gemini: `gemini/engine/schedule/schedule.py`] | lead |
| `missing_value` on `params.dN.riser.esp_depth` | pump depth not stated | the well engineer chooses it (4.3); never the lead | W |
| Plant file refused for a case value | a site or network value written in the plant | remove it; it belongs to the case (11.1) | lead |
| Tear stream with no first guess (a closed loop) | a loop module lacks the values that let it offer its outlet; for a `Cooler`: `loop_pressure` and `flow` [gemini 0.6.17] | set those values on the module the message names | the module's group |
| `inlet 'X': <error>` | the value at that inlet is invalid [gemini 0.6.17] | fix the value the message names; an inlet is `<module>.<port>` (QA-083) | lead |
| Pipe `PhysicsError`: outlet pressure below zero | friction and static drop exceed the inlet pressure | wider pipe (2.5: 1 to 3 m/s), shorter pipe, or higher loop pressure; check the flow [gemini: `gemini/modules/piping/pipe.py`] | lead |
| `bound` on `intake_pressure` or `intake_gas_fraction` | pump too shallow for the drawdown, too much flow per well, or a deep design | set the pump deeper, lower the flow per doublet and add one, wider well, higher wellhead pressure (4.3, 4.4) | W |
| ESP `out_of_range` with a `curve` | the ESP curves do not cover the flows run | the well engineer gives sourced curves, or `pump_type` `"unspecified"` with no curves (the doublet derives them) | W |
| Doublet flow below the demand it should carry | the schedule runs a doublet at most at its `nominal_flow` [gemini 0.6.15] | raise `nominal_flow` up to the case's flow cap, or add a doublet | R |
| Heat pump: no duty, source below the minimum | brine at or below `minimum_source_outlet_temperature`, or lift below the minimum | move the heat pump upstream in the cascade, lower the exchanger duty before it, check the limit (6.4, 0.8) | H |
| Unit off below its minimum part load | machine too large for a low-demand step | smaller or two units, or accept and cover by backup (9.2) | H or C |
| Absorption chiller delivers nothing | drive water below `minimum_driving_temperature`, or cooling water too warm | hotter drive water (first in the cascade), larger cooler, or another chiller (7.2) | C |
| `heat_delivered` / `cold_delivered` fails | too little capacity on peak or outage days | read the worst step; add boiler or chiller capacity; check the backup policy covers outage days (8.4, 8.5) | H (C for cold) |
| `brine_cooling_limit` fails | brine cooled beyond the cap | heat pump `minimum_source_outlet_temperature` = production temperature less the cap, or a smaller heat pump (0.8) | H |
| `running_time_limit` fails | a doublet runs more days than allowed | `params.control.outages` `lowest_demand`, a second doublet, backup that covers the days off (8.5) | lead; H |
| `numerical` reason | a loop that does not close, or a colder return mixed into a fixed-temperature supply | plan where each stream goes (skill `designing-a-plant`, "What gemini can run") | lead |
| Supply temperature rule fails on zero-demand days | a rule with `when: always` | a case change: the rule holds only while that supply runs (9.4); never force circulation | case lead |
| `internal` error from a tool | an input gemini did not anticipate | change the input; never repeat the same call | lead |

| Kind of value | Examples | Comes from | Ask the user? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Case value | demand, supply temperatures, gradient, permeability, prices, requirements, the time axis | the case (`read_case`); the case lead set it from the user's files, Knowledge and the user's answers | never from design: hand over `case change needed: <path>: <why>` |
| Equipment design value | well diameter, roughness, heat transfer coefficient, efficiencies, COP model, UA, pipe size, cooler approach, treatment values | 0.7 first; then one `search_knowledge` / `search_rag`; else your engineering choice with a one-line reason; record as an assumption `{id, text, value, source, confirmed: false}` | no; never ask for a datasheet, a pump curve or stage coefficients |
| Equipment operating limit | ESP minimum intake pressure and maximum gas fraction, minimum drive temperature, minimum part load | as an equipment value; keep it on every unit (4.4, 10.4) | no |
| Plant rule | `params.control.dispatch`, `params.control.outages` | the one value gemini's `suggestions` give (0.5) | no |
| Lead's decision | backup policy, objective, number of evaluations, seed, family | the lead, as an assumption with its reason | no |
| Network length and layout | the length, diameter and elevation of the pipes to the consumers when the plant models the network | the case, its files or its assumptions document in Knowledge; never invented | yes, when none gives it: hand over `case change needed: <path>: network length not given`, so the case lead asks the user |
| Search range or option | `size.doublets` 1 to 3, `dN.nominal_flow`, `depth`, capacities | the user or the case (a range the plant file states, a requirement such as the doublet count) | yes, when missing: `ask_user` with the proposed values and a reason; `set_ranges` only after the answer |

## 0.7 Design values: meaning, unit, how to choose

The plant paths gemini asks for when a plant is built from a class, grouped by engineer. `dN` is
each doublet (`d0`, `d1`, ...). Write each with its unit as `{"value": 0.244, "unit": "m"}`; a
dimensionless value is a number (skill `gemini-units`). The last column gives a published value
where one exists; otherwise the value is an engineering choice: take it from the case's own
assumptions document in Knowledge when there is one (search it once by the path), else choose it
with a one-line reason and record it as an assumption (0.6).

**Doublet, wells and reservoir (R: reservoir values; W: `depth`, wells, wellhead)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `depth` (`dN.depth` on a free plant) | true vertical depth of the reservoir midpoint | m | the case's reservoir depth, or searched within a range the user approves (3.6) | — |
| `dN.nominal_flow` | design flow per doublet; the schedule never runs a doublet above it | m3/h | the case's flow cap; `size_plant` sets it (12.5) | — |
| `dN.well_diameter` | inner diameter of the production casing | m | friction and pump size (4.1, 4.2) | 9 5/8 in or 7 in production casing is common [Stober and Bucher 2013] |
| `dN.drainage_radius` | drainage radius of the Darcy productivity; enters by a logarithm (3.3) | m | about half the spacing between doublets | doublet spacing about 1 to 2 km [Willems 2016] |
| `dN.roughness` | wall roughness of the wells | m | new steel; more with scale and corrosion | 4.5e-5 for new commercial steel [Moody 1944] |
| `dN.pump_efficiency` | production pump efficiency | 1 | the case's value when it states one, else the pump's (4.5) | — |
| `dN.nominal_wellhead_pressure` | production wellhead pressure at design flow | bar | high enough to keep gas in solution in the surface loop (5.1) and to reach the injector | — |
| `dN.reservoir.skin`, `dN.sink.skin` | near-well skin of producer and injector | 1 | 0 for a new well is optimistic for an injector (3.3) | — |
| `dN.reservoir.decline_threshold`, `dN.sink.decline_threshold` | alarm threshold of decline | 1 | the share of decline that should raise an alarm | — |
| `dN.well/riser/injector.friction_correlation`, `two_phase_friction_correlation` | friction models | text | single phase `darcy_weisbach`; two phase `BeggsBrill` where gas comes out (4.2) | — |
| `dN.well/riser/injector.heat_transfer_coefficient` | heat loss of the brine to the rock | W/m2/K | of the order of 10 for a cased well; a low value keeps the wellhead close to the reservoir temperature (3.1) | — |

## The tools

### `list_files`

List the files of the project: `files`, each with `name`, `size` and `media_type`.

Read one with `read_rag`, and give a data file to the case with `set_case` `files`.

### `read_rag`

Read a project file, or a document of the knowledge base as `knowledge/<name>`, as text.

A long document with headings (a handbook of 25 to 50 pages with `#`, `##`, `###`) is read by
section, never page by page from the start:

- `read_rag(name, outline=true)`: the heading tree, each `{level, number, title, start, size}`
  (`number` is the title's own, such as `3.2`, else its place in the tree).
- `read_rag(name, section="3.2")` or `section="Pumps"` (a title, or a part of one): exactly that
  section with its subsections, paged with `start` inside it when it is longer than a page; the
  answer names the `section` read. An unknown section is refused with the headings it has.
- A knowledge hit of `search_rag` carries `section`, the heading path it falls in
  (`3 Wells > 3.2 Pumps`): read that whole section next with `section`.

CSV, TSV, JSON, Markdown and text files read as they are, and a PDF as its extracted text with
a `[page n]` marker before each page; another file is a `not_text` error. `start` is the
first character and `length` the number of characters, at most 20,000. Returns `name`,
`start`, `total`, `text` and `next`, where the following page starts (`null` at the
end). The first page of a CSV or TSV also has `table`: `columns`, the number of `rows`,
the `first_rows`, the `last_row` and the `span` its first column covers as a case's
time: `start`, `end` (exclusive, one step after the last row) and `step`, or `null`
when that column is not evenly spaced times. `columns` reads only those columns of a CSV or
TSV, in that order, such as the `id`, `path` and price of a cost table: a wide table costs
far fewer tokens so. `rows` (`{column: [text, ...]}`) reads only the rows whose value in
each named column starts with one of the texts, such as the paths of the keys a case lacks.
A CSV or TSV still longer than 20,000 characters after them gives no `text`: its `table`
outline and a `note`; find its rows with `search_rag` and read them by `rows`. A page
this run already read comes back as `already_read` with a `note` instead of its text: its
text is in the conversation, even with `force`, unless a compaction summarized it since;
after one, `force` reads it again until the whole document was read, then every page is
`already_read` with the references of the stored results. Nested runs share what the run
tree read.

### `search_rag`

Search the project's documents and files and the knowledge base; return `{matches, note}`.

Each match has `scope` (`project` or `knowledge`), `text`, `score` and `citation`,
what a value taken from it is cited with. A project document: `id` and `title`; a passage
of a project file that reads as text, such as a PDF: `name` and `start` for `read_rag`,
cited with its `file` and `page`; a passage of the knowledge base: `name` as
`knowledge/<document>` for `read_rag`, cited with its `document`, `title` and
`page`. The best of each scope come first, in turn. A file's name alone matches nothing. No
match means neither states these words, and the `note` says what to do instead; the same
words again are noted too. A value from the knowledge base goes into the case only after the
user confirms it, as any value no project file gives.

### `search_knowledge`

Search the global Knowledge base only (never the project's files); returns `{matches}`, each
with `name` (`knowledge/<name>`), `text`, `score`, `citation` and its `section` when it has
one. For a team's sub-agent: the lead gives you the project's text; the Knowledge base is yours
to search for what that text lacks.

## Parallel instances

A team tool (`geoscientists`, `fill_parts`) runs its briefs at the same time. Its `briefs` is
either `{member: task}`, one run per member, or a list of `{role, task}`, one run per entry, so
several instances of one role work at once. Each instance is named `<Role> <Roman numeral>`
(`Geoscientist I`, `Geoscientist II`) and its answer comes back under that name.

- At most 4 briefs in one call. Only you, the lead, read and write the project's files, case,
  plants, studies and results; the instances have no tools for them. Put into each brief
  everything it needs (the text of the pages, the values, the keys it owns). Two instances
  never work on the same key.
- Send every brief in ONE call: the instances run together, and the call ends when the last
  one answers.
- Read every answer, merge them and write ONCE; split what is still missing or disagrees among
  the team again, and repeat until done. Then report to your lead.

- The design team (`fill_parts`, roles `reservoir_engineer`, `well_engineer`,
  `energy_systems_engineer`): one brief per module group, holding the plant paths with gemini's
  issue text, the plant text of those modules, the case values with units and the settled
  interface values. Each engineer returns a proposal: `changes` `[{path, value, source,
  reason}]`, `evaluations` `[{module, point, why}]` (numbers only gemini gives: run them with
  `evaluate_module`), `case_changes` and `couplings`. Settle the couplings, then put every
  engineer's `changes` into ONE `patch_plant` (its list form takes them as they are).

Example: `geoscientists(briefs=[{"role": "geoscientist", "task": "Ground and reservoir
(site.ground.*, site.reservoir.*). Text of report.pdf pages 10-14: ..."}, {"role":
"geoscientist", "task": "Brine and dissolved gas (utilities.brine.*, utilities.gas.*). Text of
fluid.pdf pages 2-5: ..."}])`.

With `options` the user picks one option's value or types an answer of their own, which
comes back marked as typed. To ask for something typed (a path, a number with its unit, a
name), ask without options. Every answer is kept in the problem state as a confirmed user
assumption (`answer.<id>`) that every later agent reads: read the state first and never ask
a question it already answers; act on that answer instead.

### `finish`

End the run with the final answer.

### `read_skill`

Return the instructions of one skill, by its name in the system prompt.

`<skill>/<file>` reads a file the skill names.

when a requirement of the case judges it, case_requirement: that requirement's name. An
assumption has id, text, value, source (user, agent or default) and confirmed; a result id,
summary, reference; a question id, text. A rejected change names the shape expected there.'}

The plant paths gemini asks for when a plant is built from a class, grouped by engineer. `dN` is
each doublet (`d0`, `d1`, ...). Write each with its unit as `{"value": 0.244, "unit": "m"}`; a
dimensionless value is a number (skill `gemini-units`). The last column gives a published value
where one exists; otherwise the value is an engineering choice: take it from the case's own
assumptions document in Knowledge when there is one (search it once by the path), else choose it
with a one-line reason and record it as an assumption (0.6).

**Doublet, wells and reservoir (R: reservoir values; W: `depth`, wells, wellhead)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `depth` (`dN.depth` on a free plant) | true vertical depth of the reservoir midpoint | m | the case's reservoir depth, or searched within a range the user approves (3.6) | — |
| `dN.nominal_flow` | design flow per doublet; the schedule never runs a doublet above it | m3/h | the case's flow cap; `size_plant` sets it (12.5) | — |
| `dN.well_diameter` | inner diameter of the production casing | m | friction and pump size (4.1, 4.2) | 9 5/8 in or 7 in production casing is common [Stober and Bucher 2013] |
| `dN.drainage_radius` | drainage radius of the Darcy productivity; enters by a logarithm (3.3) | m | about half the spacing between doublets | doublet spacing about 1 to 2 km [Willems 2016] |
| `dN.roughness` | wall roughness of the wells | m | new steel; more with scale and corrosion | 4.5e-5 for new commercial steel [Moody 1944] |
| `dN.pump_efficiency` | production pump efficiency | 1 | the case's value when it states one, else the pump's (4.5) | — |
| `dN.nominal_wellhead_pressure` | production wellhead pressure at design flow | bar | high enough to keep gas in solution in the surface loop (5.1) and to reach the injector | — |
| `dN.reservoir.skin`, `dN.sink.skin` | near-well skin of producer and injector | 1 | 0 for a new well is optimistic for an injector (3.3) | — |
| `dN.reservoir.decline_threshold`, `dN.sink.decline_threshold` | alarm threshold of decline | 1 | the share of decline that should raise an alarm | — |
| `dN.well/riser/injector.friction_correlation`, `two_phase_friction_correlation` | friction models | text | single phase `darcy_weisbach`; two phase `BeggsBrill` where gas comes out (4.2) | — |
| `dN.well/riser/injector.heat_transfer_coefficient` | heat loss of the brine to the rock | W/m2/K | of the order of 10 for a cased well; a low value keeps the wellhead close to the reservoir temperature (3.1) | — |

**Pumps (W)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dN.riser.esp_depth` | ESP setting depth | m | asked only for a well split at its pump (`segment` `below_esp` / `above_esp`); a designed `Doublet` derives it. The shallowest depth that keeps the intake above its minimum at the largest flow and the lowest pressure; check with `evaluate_module` (4.3) [gemini: `gemini/engine/check.py`] | — |
| `dN.esp.pump_type` | pump curves | text | `"unspecified"` with no curves when no source gives a curve: the doublet derives them | — |
| `dN.esp.minimum_intake_pressure` | lowest intake pressure the pump may see | bar | above the bubble point when PVT data exist (4.3) | no general figure |
| `dN.esp.maximum_gas_fraction` | largest free gas share at the intake | 1 | the pump stage's limit (4.4) | 0.1875 for standard stages (one fourth of the 75 % of gas handlers) [Baker Hughes] |
| `dN.esp.motor_efficiency` | ESP motor efficiency | 1 | 1 when the case's pump efficiency already holds the whole loss | — |
| `injection_pump.efficiency` | injection pump efficiency | 1 | as the production pump | — |
| `injection_pump.nominal_flow`, `nominal_head` | injection pump rating | m3/h, bar | `size_plant` sets them (4.7) | — |

**Treatment and gas (R)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `degasser.separation_efficiency` | share of free gas removed | 1 | vessel design (5.2) | — |
| `degasser.nominal_pressure_drop` | pressure loss of the vessel | Pa | vendor; a fraction of a bar | — |
| `filters.<f>.nominal_pressure_drop`, `nominal_mass_flow` | clean filter loss at its flow | Pa, kg/s | the flow through it; vendor loss | — |
| `filters.<f>.clogging_pressure_drop` | loss at which the filter counts as clogged | Pa | vendor; of the order of 0.5 bar | — |
| `desander.separation_efficiency`, `nominal_pressure_drop` | hydrocyclone | 1, Pa | particle size against cut size (5.4) | loss of the order of 1 bar [Svarovsky 2000] |
| `dosing.dose`, `dosing.product_concentration` | inhibitor dose, active share | ppm, 1 | geochemistry (5.3) | doses a few to tens of ppm [Gallup 2009] |
| `flare.combustion_efficiency` | share of methane burned | 1 | flare type | 0.98 [US EPA AP-42 13.5] |

**Heating (H)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `heat_exchanger.thermal_conductance` | UA; `size_plant` does not size it | W/K | from the design duty and the chosen approach, Q = UA ΔT_lm (6.1, A.8); check with `evaluate_module` | — |
| `heat_exchanger.arrangement` | flow arrangement | text | plate exchangers are close to `counterflow` | — |
| `heat_exchanger.hot_nominal_mass_flow`, `cold_nominal_mass_flow` | design flows | kg/s | brine: the doublets' flow; network: duty / (c_p (T_s − T_r)) | — |
| `heat_exchanger.fouling_threshold` | fouling alarm | 1 | the loss of UA that should raise an alarm | — |
| `heat_pump.cop_model` | COP model | text | `carnot`; `lorenz` for large glides (6.4) | — |
| `heat_pump.carnot_fraction` | real COP over Carnot COP | 1 | the machine class | about 0.5 [Frutschi 1996]; 0.4 to 0.6 [Arpagaus et al. 2018] |
| `heat_pump.minimum_temperature_lift` | lift below which the COP is capped | K | the machine class | 10, the lowest lift of the machines reviewed [Arpagaus et al. 2018] |
| `heat_pump.minimum_source_outlet_temperature` | lowest brine temperature leaving the evaporator | degC | production temperature less the case's brine cooling cap, or a chemistry limit (0.8, 12.4) | — |
| `heat_pump.supply_margin`, `boiler.supply_margin` | heating above the supply setpoint | K | small and positive to cover losses after the unit (9.4) | — |
| `heat_pump.capacity`, `boiler.capacity` | ratings | MW | `size_plant` sets them (0.4) | — |
| `boiler.efficiency` | fuel to heat | 1 | the boiler class (6.5) | — |
| pipes `length`, `inner_diameter`, `roughness`, `elevation_change`, `heat_transfer_coefficient` | plant pipes | m, m, m, m, W/m2/K | the length of a network pipe is the site's: from the case or Knowledge, else asked (0.6), never invented; the diameter for 1 to 3 m/s at the design flow (2.5) | roughness 4.5e-5 m for new steel [Moody 1944] |

**Cooling (C)**

| Path | Meaning | Unit | How to choose | Published value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compression_chiller.mode` | heat pump run as a chiller | text | `cooling` | — |
| `compression_chiller.carnot_fraction`, `minimum_temperature_lift` | as the heat pump | 1, K | as the heat pump | as the heat pump |
| `absorption_chiller.thermal_cop` | cold over drive heat | 1 | single or double effect (7.2) | about 0.7 single effect LiBr [Herold et al. 2016] |
| `absorption_chiller.minimum_driving_temperature` | drive below which it delivers nothing | K | the machine; single effect needs about 80 °C or more (7.2) | — |
| `absorption_chiller.characteristic_slope`, `minimum_driving_difference`, `rejection_coefficient`, `evaporator_coefficient`, `auxiliary_power_ratio` | characteristic equation (7.2, A.10) | W/K, K, 1, 1, 1 | the machine's data; the slope scales with capacity | [Hellmann, Schweigler and Ziegler 1999] |
| `adsorption_chiller.thermal_cop` | cold over drive heat | 1 | the machine | about 0.55 [Wang and Oliveira 2006] |
| `adsorption_chiller.minimum_driving_temperature`, `maximum_driving_temperature` | drive window | K | the machine (7.3) | — |
| `<cooler>.cooler_type`, `approach` | dry or wet; outlet above the air (dry) or wet-bulb (wet) temperature | text, K | climate and water (7.6) | dry 5 to 15 K, wet 3 to 8 K [ASHRAE] |
| `<cooler>.specific_fan_power` | fan power over duty | 1 | a small share (7.6) | — |
| `<cooler>.capacity` | heat rejected: cold plus drive | MW | compression: cold × (1 + 1/COP); absorption at COP 0.7: about 2.4 × cold (7.2) | — |
| `<cooler>.loop_pressure`, `flow`, `temperature_setpoint` | condenser loop; a closed loop needs them for its first guess (0.5) | bar, kg/s, degC | flow = capacity / (c_p ΔT of the loop); setpoint below the chiller's condensing limit | — |

## The tools

### `optimize`

Search a stored design for the values that minimise a metric; store the best as `name`.

`objective` is a metric such as `lcts`, `lcoh`, `lcoc`, `annualised_cost` or `co2`;
a leading `-` maximises it. The variables are the ranges and options of the design (set them
with `set_ranges`); a design with none is gemini's error. The constraints are the case's
requirements, which the user owns. `evaluations` and `seed` have no default. `name`
names the stored best design and the study `study/<name>` that records the call; a taken
name is refused. Returns the `best` (its value, parameters and plant, in display units),
`feasible`, the `trials` run, the stored `design` and the `study` key. When no trial
is feasible the best is the least violating one and its `reason` says why. A search that
takes longer than 15 minutes comes back as a `timeout` error: ask for fewer evaluations.

### `simulate`

Simulate a plant on the state's case and store the results; return a reference and summary.

`design` is a stored design (`design/<name>`); `plant_version` is a saved plant version of the
project (`list_plants` project_versions), never with `design`. With neither, it runs the
project's LATEST plant version, and the summary's `plant` names that version: to report on an
older version, pass its `plant_version`.
`changes` holds parameters by module path for this run only, each a `{"value", "unit"}`
(a dimensionless parameter may be a number); the plant's own options go under `control`
(`{"control": {"dispatch": {"value": "least_cost"}}}`) or as `backup`. `start` and `end` are ISO 8601 times that cut
the case's time to a window, both inclusive: the run, its summary and its stored case are those
of the window (the case's `time` cut to it); to change the case's time itself use set_case.

The plan comes from gemini's schedule over the case. A step that fails is a failed row in the
summary and the run goes on. What `gm.check` finds wrong with the plant on this case (a
parameter without a value, equipment without a cost in the economics, a role a requirement
names) is a gemini error with each issue's path and message, and nothing runs.

The summary gives the steps, the failed steps with their first groups, the report's totals in
display units (MWh, MEUR, EUR/MWh, kt), gemini's `verdict`, the requirements that are not met
(`unmet`), the coverage of the demand, the plant and the case's time span.

### `size_plant`

Size a stored design for the state's case; store the sized plant as design `name`.

Sizing reads the plant's ranges (`size.doublets` min and max, when its class takes doublets)
and its `params.backup`; set what is missing with `set_ranges` first. The boiler's backup
policy is the plant's own `params.backup`: `peak` covers the whole heating peak with
the doublets off, `none` covers only what the doublets cannot reach. The policy has no
default: set it in the plant first, as an assumption when the user gave none. `name` names
the sized design and the study `study/<name>` that records the call; a taken name is
refused. Returns the new design reference, the `study` key,
gemini's notes (what was `sized` with its reason, what stayed `unchanged`, what is
`broken` and the `simulation` that judged it) and, as `patch_plant` gives them, the
sized plant's `issues` with their count `missing`: every value `simulate` still needs.'}
